prompt: Which Antminer firmware has the best autotuning for efficiency (J/TH)? Compare vendors.
answer_text:
When optimizing Antminer efficiency (measured in joules per terahash, J/TH), several custom firmware options offer autotuning features that adjust each chip's frequency and voltage for optimal performance. The primary vendors providing such firmware are VNISH, Braiins OS+, and LuxOS. Here's a comparison of their autotuning capabilities:

| Feature                 | VNISH                                                                                   | Braiins OS+                                                                                 | LuxOS                                                                                   |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Autotuning Method**   | Per-chip autotuning: calibrates each chip individually for optimal efficiency. ([vni.sh](https://vni.sh/autotune?utm_source=openai)) | Per-chip autotuning: analyzes each chip to find the best voltage-frequency combination. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) | Per-board autotuning: adjusts settings for each board as a whole. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Efficiency Gains**    | Typically 5%–15% improvement in efficiency. ([coinwebmining.com](https://coinwebmining.com/vnish-firmware-guide/?utm_source=openai)) | Typically 10%–20% improvement in efficiency. ([rax.ae](https://rax.ae/knowledge-center/articles/asic-firmware-optimization-mining-efficiency.html?utm_source=openai)) | Typically 8%–18% improvement in efficiency. ([rax.ae](https://rax.ae/knowledge-center/articles/asic-firmware-optimization-mining-efficiency.html?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Supported Models**    | Wide range, including S9 through S21 series and L7/L9. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) | S9 through S21 series. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) | S19 and S21 series. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Development Fee**     | 2–2.8% of hashrate, depending on the pool used. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) | 2–2.5% of hashrate, with potential rebates on Braiins Pool. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) | 2.8% of hashrate, with potential rebates on Luxor Pool. ([d-central.tech](https://d-central.tech/antminer-firmware-update-guide/?utm_source=openai)) |

In summary, VNISH, Braiins OS+, and LuxOS all offer autotuning features that can enhance Antminer efficiency. VNISH and Braiins OS+ provide per-chip autotuning, which may offer more precise optimization, while LuxOS employs per-board autotuning. Efficiency gains vary among them, with Braiins OS+ generally offering the highest improvements. Consider your specific hardware model, desired efficiency gains, and the development fees when choosing the most suitable firmware for your needs.
